'SELECT max(row) FROM <keyed leaf>' returns n; each leaf's node_id is the node's address as digits, its old hash is in legacy_node_id, its table tag came from the tag registry at 0x0100 or above, and the node's in list holds that leaf's address; each leaf's leaf_id is rewritten to trees.leaf_id_for(address, new eid), or leaf_id_for(address, key) for a keyed leaf, the old one kept in an additive legacy_leaf_id column / embeddings and links follow: each legacy embedding whose node maps lands in cairn_mem_embeddings with embedding_id = trees.embedding_id_for(address, render_method) and the node's address (the legacy row stays untouched in cairn_embeddings, its old id readable there); each legacy link lands as one link row through trees.link with its weight and traversals kept; and re-depositing already-migrated content after --write moves neither the embedding count nor the leaf count / nothing is dropped: the legacy nodes, embeddings and links tables keep their row counts and contents through --write; a leaf table keeps its row count; an embedding, link or leaf whose hash maps to no node is named by id in the report and left untouched / content already held at an address (a deposit made after T2 landed) maps the legacy hash onto that address and appends the legacy provenance as an attestation; no second node row is laid / the dry run writes nothing (every new and legacy table's row count is unchanged), and a second --write lays no row, column, index or tag.
